subject: Post-call: pricing follow-up & regional residency (US vs EU)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-02-25T15:12:00-05:00
Subject: Post-call: pricing follow-up & regional residency (US vs EU)

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and the few items we promised to follow up on: 

1) Monthly token volumes: you mentioned a phased rollout starting at ~25M tokens/month for Q2 with a target of ~1B tokens within 12 months. Can you confirm the expected ramp (month-by-month) and the % of that traffic that will be EU-resident vs US?

2) Residency & compliance: you indicated EU data residency is required for payment data and some user PII. Can you confirm if the whole inference payload needs to stay in the EU or only a subset (e.g., payment tokens)? Also, any specific certs beyond SOC 2 we should consider?

3) Budget / unit economics: procurement asked for guidance on target spend. Can you share the budget range you have for inference (ballpark $/month or $/1M tokens)? If it helps, we're preparing back-of-envelope unit costs (by model and region) and can propose options to hit a target $/1M tokens.

Next steps: I'll loop in pricing to provide US vs EU unit economics and a simple 3-tier routing suggestion (EU-only, EU-pref, US-fallback). Attached is a short worksheet we use to align on target $/1M tokens — if you can populate the expected monthly volumes per region we can produce a tailored estimate.

Would next Wednesday for a pricing walkthrough work?

Cheers,
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood-pricing-1M-token-worksheet.xlsx

Hi Dylan —

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volumes: initial pilot (April) ~25M tokens/mo, May 50M, June 150M; by EOY we expect cumulative ~800M-1B tokens/mo once fully live. EU traffic is expected to be ~60%-65% of inference volume (largest product market is EMEA).

2) Residency: For payment-related inference and anything that includes payment identifiers we need EU-only processing. For general chat/assist flows EU preference is fine but we can accept US processing if we first pseudonymize payment identifiers. SOC 2 is required; additional requests: we may ask for regional data processing addendum and evidence of data residency controls.

3) Budget: Procurement asked for a target unit cost. They wrote: "target under $250 per 1M tokens for high-throughput enc+dec flows, and ideally <$150 per 1M for embeddings-heavy workloads." We know these are aggressive — happy to see what you propose.

Attachments: procurement included our vendor questionnaire and expected monthly volumes per product line — attaching for your pricing team.

Best,
Lena Park

Marissa / Sean —

Forwarding Lena's reply and procurement questionnaire (attached). Key asks to price: 
- Starting ramp: Apr 25M -> May 50M -> Jun 150M -> EOY 800M-1B
- Region split: ~60-65% EU (EU-only required for payment inference)
- Procurement target: <$250 / 1M tokens for generate flows, <$150 / 1M for embeddings-heavy.

2) Recommend a routing policy to meet procurement target while keeping payment inference EU-only (suggest model variant + fallback).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: lena.park@fintechco.com
Date: 2026-02-27T11:08:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: pricing follow-up & regional residency (US vs EU) — FintechCo numbers

Hi team and Lena —

Thanks for the details — this is a solid ramp and good to see the explicit target from procurement. High-level numbers below (ballpark, final to be confirmed in the walkthrough):

Assumptions: mixed workload (70% generation, 30% embeddings), typical gen model = 13B quanitized Q4/Q8 variant, embeddings model = s-embed-large. Pricing below quoted as $ per 1M tokens processed (generate includes both enc/dec tokens where relevant).

1) US pricing (hosted):
- Generation (13B q8): $180 per 1M tokens
- Embeddings (s-embed-large): $120 per 1M tokens

2) EU pricing (hosted EU region with residency controls):
- Generation (13B q8): $225 per 1M tokens (approx +25% uplift for EU infra & regional capacity)
- Embeddings (s-embed-large): $150 per 1M tokens (approx +25% uplift)

3) Private / Dedicated alternative (if they need hard EU-only for payment inference and want lower unit economics at scale):
- Dedicated EU pool pricing (committed): Generation ~ $140 per 1M tokens, Embeddings ~ $95 per 1M tokens — requires 6/12 month commit and predictable baseline (we can model commits to meet their EOY numbers).

Routing recommendation: 
- Route payment inference to EU-dedicated pool (EU-only processing) to satisfy residency and keep audit trail.
- Route general product traffic to EU-hosted region where possible; fall back to US-hosted only after pseudonymization for non-payment flows.
- If procurement wants to meet <$250 / 1M for gen, hosted EU ($225) is inside the target; for embeddings ($150) currently above the ideal $150 target but close. If they commit to Dedicated EU, we can reach ~$140/$95 which is comfortably below procurement targets.

Notes on unit economics: the ~25% uplift is driven by higher EU spot/nodes pricing, cross-region egress controls, and extra isolation (VPC + KMS keys). If they can accept a hybrid (payment in dedicated EU; general in hosted EU with caching/batching) we can optimize cost. Also worth modeling throttles and KV caching to lower per-token compute on repeated prompts.

Next steps: I'll join the pricing walkthrough next Wed and bring a short slide with committed vs hosted cost models. Dylan — please share the completed worksheet (region-by-product volumes). Lena — if procurement is open, we can sketch a 6-month committed plan that brings us below their targets.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
Attach: soc2-eu-data-residency.pdf
